settings.title: Global settings

llm.tokenHint: Generate one with `claude setup-token`. It is kept in the OS credential store.
llm.tokenDesktopOnly: Only available in the desktop app.
llm.tokenError: Could not access the credential store: {{error}}
llm.accountsHint: Add one or more setup tokens (personal subscriptions). Runs use them in turn; an account that hits a limit rests and the run moves to the next.

modeHint.round_robin: Each run takes the next account in turn.
modeHint.drain: Always uses the first available account until Claude says it hit its limit, then moves on to the next one.

images.intro: What agents run on. The base image is built in; add your own with a script on top of it. A profile picks the image.
images.baseDescription: Alpine with agentd, Claude Code and ripgrep. Built by the app, it cannot be edited. Rebuilt after an app update that changes it.
images.scriptHint: Runs once as root on top of the parent image (Alpine, apk available). Saving builds it.
images.needBase: Build the image it is based on first.
images.parentHint: The image the script runs on. Rebuilding it makes this one out of date.
images.envHint: Baked into the image and its children, in plain text: no secrets.
images.docs: Tool docs for the system prompt
images.docsHint: Appended to the system prompt of every agent on this image. A command runs once at build time and its output is saved (e.g. jira --help); text is added as written. Keep it short: it is sent with every run.
images.docTextPlaceholder: ## Title, or a few lines of advice

network.intro: Hosts every agent may reach over HTTPS. Profiles can add more. No other network access.
network.allowHostsHint: One per line: a name (github.com) or its subdomains (*.github.com). Everything else is blocked. An empty list cuts agents off from the Claude API.
network.webhookPortHint: Webhook nodes listen on this port on this computer only (127.0.0.1). The secret in each URL authorizes a call.
network.projectIntro: Hosts every agent of this project may reach over HTTPS, on top of the global and profile ones. An entry may be a ${var:NAME}.
network.maxConnectionsHint: Tunnels one agent may have open at once. A profile can set its own.
network.leakHint: Refuses a request that carries one of an agent's environment secrets to a host its profile does not list. This inspects the TLS traffic of those runs.

secrets.intro: Values kept in the OS credential store. Use one in a profile's environment as ${secret:NAME}; it reaches the agent's environment, so use least-privilege tokens.
secrets.desktopOnly: Secrets are only available in the desktop app.
secrets.newHint: A name and a value. Values cannot be read back, only replaced.
secrets.badName: Letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit.

variables.intro: Named values that are not secret, such as a site's address. Use one as ${var:NAME} in a profile's environment or an injection's host or user name. Saved in plain text: put secrets in Secrets.
variables.desktopOnly: Variables are only available in the desktop app.
variables.newHint: A name (letters, digits, underscore) and its value, on one line.
variables.badName: Letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit.

injections.intro: Credentials the app adds to an agent's requests to certain hosts, so the secret never enters the VM. Use one as ${injection:NAME} in a profile's environment; the host must be in its allowed hosts.
injections.desktopOnly: Injections are only available in the desktop app.
injections.name: Name
injections.nameHint: Letters, digits and underscores. It cannot be changed later.
injections.rulesHint: Host (api.example.com or *.example.com), path pattern (* matches anything; empty = all) and methods (none = all). HTTPS only.
injections.usernameHint: Pick a variable or a secret from the list, or type a fixed name
injections.noVariables: Create the variable in Variables first.
injections.textHint: Saved in plain text, visible here: not for credentials. Use a secret for those.
injections.noSecrets: Create the secret in Settings > Secrets first.
injections.placeholderHint: What the agent sees in its variable. Make it look like a token if a tool checks the format. Default: ccaf-injected.

settings.notifications: Desktop notifications when a session needs me or ends
settings.globalIntro: Global settings apply to every project: Claude accounts, the base image and the hosts every agent needs.
settings.globalNote: Global: available in every project. A project's own item with the same name wins.

integrations.intro: A service your agents use (Jira, GitHub), set up in one place: variables, secrets, injections, hosts and environment. Pick it in an agent profile.
integrations.desktopOnly: Integrations are only available in the desktop app.
integrations.name: Name
integrations.variablesHint: Plain values that are not secret (a site's host, an e-mail address).
integrations.secretsHint: Write-only: the value goes to the OS credential store and is never shown again.
integrations.injectionsHint: The app adds the secret to requests that match the host and path; the agent only sees a placeholder.
integrations.hostsHint: Hosts the agent may reach. List the host of every injection above.
integrations.envHint: Added to every profile that uses this integration. Pick a reference or type a value.

transfer.desktopOnly: Import and export are only available in the desktop app.
transfer.exportIntro: Saves everything as one encrypted YAML file: all projects, global settings, profiles, workflows, image definitions, secrets and Claude tokens. Not included: session logs, built image disks and app preferences.
transfer.exportWarning: The file contains your secrets and tokens. The password is the only protection and cannot be recovered: keep both safe.
transfer.passwordHint: At least {{min}} characters. It is the encryption key.
transfer.importIntro: Reads an export file and adds its content. Nothing is deleted. Images are imported as definitions: build them afterwards. Restart the app to apply a changed webhook port.
transfer.overwrite: Replace items that already exist (otherwise they stay as they are)
transfer.imported: Imported: {{written}} files, {{secrets}} secrets, {{tokens}} Claude tokens; {{skipped}} left as they were.

vm.title: Virtual machines

accelHint.auto: Uses KVM, HVF or WHPX when the computer has it, else slow software emulation.
accelHint.hardware: A VM that cannot get hardware acceleration fails instead of running very slowly.
accelHint.software: Always emulated: very slow. For debugging or a broken hypervisor.

vm.defaultCpusHint: For profiles that set none. Empty: the host's cores, at most 4.
vm.defaultMemoryHint: What a new agent profile starts with.
vm.graceHint: Added to an agent's timeout for its VM to boot and shut down.
vm.imageScriptHint: How long an image build script may run.

updates.title: Updates
updates.managed: Version {{version}} is available. This install is managed by your package manager.
updates.ready: Version {{version}} was installed. Restart to use it.

profiles.title: Agent profiles
profiles.empty: No agent profiles yet. Create one to define how an agent is set up.
profiles.desktopOnly: Only available in the desktop app.
profiles.name: Name
profiles.systemPromptHint: Added to Claude's system prompt for every task of this agent.
profiles.envHint: Sent to the agent with every task. A value can be ${secret:NAME}, ${injection:NAME} (the VM sees only a placeholder) or ${var:NAME}.
profiles.imageHint: The system this agent runs on. Images are managed in Settings.
profiles.effortHint: How much the agent thinks before answering. Higher is slower and uses more tokens.
profiles.cpusHint: Virtual CPUs of the VM. Empty = the host's cores, at most 4.
profiles.memoryHint: RAM of the VM, at least 1024. Default 2048.
profiles.allowHostsHint: Hosts this agent may reach over HTTPS, one per line (github.com or *.github.com; ${var:NAME} works). Added to the global ones. List the host of every injection it uses.
profiles.secretWarning: {{names}} gets a secret in plain text: the value reaches the VM's environment, where the agent (and anything it runs) can read and send it. Prefer an injection (Settings > Injections): the VM then only sees a placeholder and the proxy adds the real credential.
profiles.integrationsHint: Each integration adds its environment and hosts to this agent. Set them up under Integrations.
profiles.maxConnectionsHint: Tunnels this agent may have open at once. Empty uses the global limit (Settings > Network).
profiles.dataBudgetHint: Sent (↑) and received (↓) over the whole run. It includes the traffic to the Claude API. When one is used up the connections close and the run stops. Empty means no limit.

welcome.text: Set up demo content? It creates a demo project: three images (built in the background), seven agent profiles, dummy secrets and injections for GitHub and Jira, and the standard delivery workflow (orchestrator → project manager → analyst, architect, developer, reviewer, tester). You can edit or delete all of it later.
welcome.done: Demo content created. The images are building.
welcome.step1Text: Pick how the app looks and speaks. You can change both later in Settings.
welcome.step0Text: CC Agent Flows runs teams of Claude Code agents that deliver work end to end. You write a request in a session; the agents of a workflow hand work to each other, each in its own sandboxed VM with no secrets inside and only the network hosts you allow. They use your Claude subscription, no API keys.

sessions.intro: A session runs the workflow for a request you write in chat.

wf.pick: An arrow from A to B means A may hand work to B. The agent nobody hands work to is the root and receives the user's request; an agent with arrows coordinates the agents it points to and decides what to hand out, in what order and how often. Drag from an agent's right handle to another agent to connect them; select an arrow to require approval.
wf.coordinates: Coordinates {{count}} agent(s): decides what to delegate and when it is done.
wf.worker: Does its work and reports; calls no one.
wf.label: Label
wf.agentPromptHint: What this agent does here. Coordinators also use it to decide order and loops.
wf.maxCallsHint: How many times this agent may be called in a session. Bounds loops.
wf.timeoutHint: How long one run of this agent may take before it is killed. Default 30.

problem.no_root: No agent is the root: every agent is called by another (a cycle).
problem.many_roots: More than one agent is not called by anyone; exactly one root is needed.
problem.unreachable: "{{node}}" cannot be reached from the root.
problem.unknown_profile: "{{node}}" uses an agent profile that does not exist.
problem.human_unused: "{{node}}" has no arrow pointing to it.
problem.gate_no_target: The approval gate "{{node}}" leads nowhere: draw an arrow from it to an agent.
problem.trigger_no_target: A trigger points to no agent.
problem.cron_no_request: A schedule needs the request it starts sessions with.
problem.no_chat_entry: The chat node points to no agent.

kindHint.ask: An agent with an arrow to this node may put its questions to the user directly, instead of passing them up to whoever called it.
kindHint.approve: Put it on the way between two agents (A to gate to B): each time A wants to hand work to B, the user approves or rejects. Asked even when the session never lets agents ask questions.
kindHint.chat: The user's chat message starts the session. Point it at the agent that should receive the messages (without a chat node, the root does).
kindHint.cron: Starts a session on a schedule, with the request below, for the agent this points to. The app must be running at that time.
kindHint.webhook: Starts a session when its URL gets a request. The body, exactly as it arrives, becomes the request of the agent this points to.

edgeKindHint.delegate: The first may hand work to the second (or ask the user, if the second is the user).
edgeKindHint.before: Between two agents called by the same coordinator: the second can be called only after the first has finished. The coordinator is held to it; it may still call them again later (loops).

wf.intro: The agents and who may hand work to whom. A session runs this workflow for a request you write in chat.
wf.instructionsHint: Added to the system prompt of every agent, before its profile's own.
wf.name: Name
wf.triggerOneAgent: A trigger hands the request to one agent.
wf.cronHint: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, local time. E.g. 0 9 * * 1-5; also @daily.
wf.cronRequestHint: What the session is asked to do each time.
wf.webhookTextHint: Optional instructions placed before the body, for example "Handle this event." The body itself is passed on unchanged.
wf.triggerAutonomyHint: Nobody watches these sessions, so the usual choice is that agents decide on their own.
wf.saveFirst: Save the workflow to see the details and try it.
wf.webhookUrlHint: Send a request to it (any method). Treat it like a password: anyone with the URL can start sessions.

reset.title: Reset to demo content?
reset.images: The starter images (manager, developer, qa) are written again with their original script and settings; your edits to them are lost. Images you made yourself are not touched. The ones that end up out of date are rebuilt.
reset.profiles: The starter profiles (orchestrator, project manager, business analyst, architect, developer, reviewer, qa) are written again as they were first created, with their prompts, variables and allowed hosts; your edits to them are lost and deleted ones come back. Other profiles are not touched.
reset.secrets: GITHUB_TOKEN, GITHUB_READONLY_TOKEN and JIRA_TOKEN are set to the dummy value again. If you stored real tokens under these names, they are lost. Other secrets are not touched.
reset.variables: ATLASSIAN_HOST and ATLASSIAN_EMAIL are set to their placeholder values again. If you entered your own, they are lost. Other variables are not touched.
reset.injections: The injections GITHUB, GITHUB_READONLY and JIRA are written again as they were first created; your edits to them are lost. Other injections are not touched.

analytics.intro: Tokens, time and failures over your sessions, from their logs.

projects.title: Projects
projects.intro: A project holds its own workflows, sessions, profiles, images, variables, secrets and injections, plus allowed hosts and a system prompt.
projects.empty: No projects yet. Create one, or set up the demo project.
projects.demoHint: The demo project is a ready-made delivery pipeline: images, agent profiles, secrets, injections and a workflow.
projects.systemPrompt: System prompt for all the project's agents
projects.systemPromptHint: Given to every agent of the project, before the workflow's instructions and the profile's own system prompt.
projects.deleteText: This deletes the project with its workflows, sessions, agent profiles, images, variables, injections and secrets. It cannot be undone.
projects.scopeNote: These belong to this project. Global ones apply too; on a name clash the project's wins.

overview.title: The idea
overview.text: You describe what you want in a session. A workflow, an org chart of agents, delivers it: coordinators decide who works next, workers do the job and report back. Everything an agent does is shown live in the session.

projects.title: Projects
projects.text: A project owns its workflows, sessions, agent profiles, images, variables, secrets, injections and allowed hosts. Global settings hold what every project shares: Claude accounts, the base image and the hosts agents always need.

agents.title: Agent profiles and images
agents.text: A profile defines an agent: system prompt, model, resources, environment and allowed hosts. It runs on an image, a disk with the tools it needs. Every run is a fresh, disposable VM.

workflow.title: Workflows
workflow.text: Boxes are agents, arrows say who may hand work to whom. Dashed arrows set an order. A You node lets agents ask you questions, an approval node asks before a handover. Chat, cron and webhook nodes start sessions.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.text: A session is one conversation with a workflow. Follow the graph, the timeline and each agent's traffic, answer questions, approve handovers, and send follow-ups. A stopped session can continue where it left off.

security.title: Safety
security.text: Agents have no network except the allowed hosts. Credentials are added by the app to matching requests (injections), so they never enter the VM. Secrets given as environment variables do reach the agent: use least-privilege tokens.

start.title: Getting started
start.text: Add a Claude token under Global settings > LLM, create a project (or the demo), check the workflow and agent profiles, then open Sessions and write your request.
